To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the effectiveness of a brief flash at eliciting shape recognition increases with the number of brief flashes, and (2) two threshold-intensity brief flashes can combine their impact for at least 50 ms.

the effectiveness of a brief flash depends on the number of brief transitions in intensity, and that the effectiveness of multiple flashes depends on the number, duration, and intensity of the flashes.

the perceptual influence of a flash of light depends not only on the quantity of photons delivered, but also on the number of flashes, the rate of the flashes, and the duration of the interstimulus intervals between the flashes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of what information is conveyed by very brief light flashes.
the question of how the visual system processes information about light intensity changes.
the question of how the brain can recognize a pattern of light in the world, even when the pattern is presented in under 200 microseconds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the perception of a brief flash is based on the quantity of photons delivered only after the flash has been processed by a neural system that is capable of recognizing the shape of the light pattern.
the perceptual effectiveness of a flash is determined by the temporal structure of the flash.
the perceptual effect of a brief light flash is not determined by the quantity or the duration of the photons delivered.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the perceptual effect of a brief flash is determined by the rate at which the intensity of light changes, not the total quantity of light.
shape recognition elicited by very brief flashes is not based solely on photon quantity.
brief flashes of light can be recognized, even when the quantity of photons is below the threshold for conscious detection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the perceptual effectiveness of brief flashes does not depend only on the quantity of photons they deliver.
it is important to understand the nature of the neural signals that are elicited by brief flashes.
the brief transitions in light intensity are the critical factor, and not the total quantity of light.
